'''Blake Carrington Wesley''' (born March 16, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]].

==Early life==
Wesley played for [[James Whitcomb Riley High School]] in [[South Bend, Indiana]]. As a junior, he averaged 26 points and 6.3 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Neddenriep |first1=Kyle |title=Riley's Wesley nets 247sports' No. 100 national ranking |url=https://www.southbendtribune.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/06/25/ileys-wesley-nets-247sports-no-100-national-ranking/116054296/ |website=[[South Bend Tribune]] |access-date=February 10, 2022 |date=June 25, 2020}}</ref> In his senior season, Wesley averaged 27.1 points, 6.1 rebounds and 2.5 steals per game, leading Riley to the Class 4A sectional title. He was named to the Indiana All-Star team.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Skol Jr. |first1=Mark |title=St. Joe’s JR Konieczny and Riley’s Blake Wesley named 2021 Indiana All-Stars |url=https://www.wndu.com/2021/04/19/st-joes-jr-konieczny-and-rileys-blake-wesley-named-2021-indiana-all-stars/ |publisher=[[WNDU-TV]] |access-date=February 10, 2022 |date=April 19, 2021}}</ref>

Wesley was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]]. On November 20, 2020, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]], choosing the Fighting Irish over offers from [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Noie |first1=Tom |title=South Bend Riley guard Blake Wesley commits to Notre Dame |url=https://www.southbendtribune.com/story/sports/college/2020/11/20/south-bend-riley-guard-blake-wesley-commits-to-notre-dame/116066578/ |website=[[South Bend Tribune]] |access-date=February 10, 2022 |date=November 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Blake-Wesley-46083365/|title=Blake Wesley|website=247sports.com|publisher=247 Sports|access-date=March 7, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
Wesley had an immediate impact during his freshman season at Notre Dame, and analysts began to consider him a first-round [[2022 NBA draft]] prospect.<ref>{{cite web |title=Notre Dame's Blake Wesley making a name for himself |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2022/01/19/notre-dames-blake-wesley-making-a-name-for-himself/49672393/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=February 10, 2022 |date=January 19, 2022}}</ref> In his college debut on November 13, 2021, he scored 21 points in a 68–52 win over [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Wesley, Goodwin propel Notre Dame past CS Northridge 68–52 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401369962 |access-date=February 10, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 13, 2021}}</ref> On November 29, 2021, Wesley scored a career-high 24 points in an 82–72 loss to [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Cockburn, Plummer lead Illinois past Notre Dame 82–72 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401369964 |access-date=February 10, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 29, 2021}}</ref> He was named to the Second Team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] as well as the All-Rookie Team.<ref name=ACCAwards>{{cite press release|url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|title=ACC Unveils 2021–22 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=March 7, 2022 |accessdate=March 7, 2022}}</ref> As a freshman, Wesley averaged 14.4 points, 3.7 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game. On March 30, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|title=Freshman Blake Wesley 'ready to start my next journey,' will leave Notre Dame to enter NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33631916/freshman-blake-wesley-ready-start-my-next-journey-leave-notre-dame-enter-nba-draft|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|date=March 30, 2022|accessdate=March 30, 2022}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===San Antonio Spurs (2022–2025)===
On June 23, 2022, Wesley was selected with the 25th pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]] by the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs select Jeremy Sochan, Malaki Branham and Blake Wesley in 2022 NBA draft|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-select-jeremy-sochan-malaki-branham-and-blake-wesley-in-2022-nba-draft|date=June 23, 2022|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 23, 2022}}</ref> Wesley joined the Spurs' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster. In his Summer League debut, Wesley scored twenty points and five assists in a 90–99 loss against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Antonio Spurs vs Cleveland Cavaliers Jul 8, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/sas-vs-cle-1522200004/box-score#box-score |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=www.nba.com}}</ref> On July 5, Wesley signed a rookie-scale contract with the Spurs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SPURS SIGN 2022 FIRST ROUND DRAFT PICK BLAKE WESLEY |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-2022-first-round-draft-pick-blake-wesley |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> Wesley made his NBA debut on October 28, scoring 10 points and 4 assists in a 129–124 win against the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Two days later, in his second career game, Wesley tore his left [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] when he collided with [[Jaden McDaniels]] during the second quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA rookie had found an early role, and groove, as backup in San Antonio |url=https://www.ndinsider.com/story/sports/mens-basketball/2022/10/31/nba-rookie-had-finally-found-his-role-with-san-antonio-before-injury/69608229007/ |access-date=2022-12-25 |website=Notre Dame Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> Wesley was assigned to the [[Austin Spurs]] on December 16, and returned to game action less than 7 weeks after his injury, scoring 12 points in a 112–102 loss to the [[Capitanes de la Ciudad de México]] on December 16.

===Portland Trail Blazers (2025–2026)===
On July 9, 2025, Wesley and [[Malaki Branham]] were traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Kelly Olynyk]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs Acquire Kelly Olynyk|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-aquire-kelly-olynyk|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2025|access-date=July 9, 2025}}</ref> On July 19, Wesley was waived by the Wizards after agreeing to a buyout.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-19 |title=Blake Wesley: Waived by Washington |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/blake-wesley-waived-by-washington/ |access-date=2025-07-19 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> On July 22, Wesley signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Blake Wesley|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-blake-wesley|website=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2025|access-date=July 22, 2025}}</ref> On November 3, Wesley suffered a fracture to the [[fifth metatarsal]] of his right foot during a game against the [[2025–26 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Trail Blazers newcomer suffers foot fracture | website=basketnews.com | date=2025-11-03 | url=https://basketnews.com/news-234271-trail-blazers-newcomer-suffers-foot-fracture.html | access-date=2025-12-03}}</ref> After undergoing surgery, he was ruled out for 8-to-12 weeks.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Blake Wesley Undergoes Successful Surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/blake-wesley-undergoes-successful-surgery?srsltid=AfmBOoqy25nvofdvKgz-Hxa_3IoHWqW0Rwhnu0uTC6Y-0EEbBXV96FSH|access-date=January 2, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref>
